questions.q: What does checking "Isolate script" on a Client Script record actually do?
options: Runs the script inside a sandboxed iframe, separate from the page's global scope and other scripts' variables
Moves the script's execution to the ServiceNow application server
Disables the script entirely until manually activated
Converts the client script into a Business Rule
questions.explain: Isolation sandboxes the script inside its own iframe context, separate from the page's shared global JavaScript.

questions.q: Two non-isolated client scripts both declare `var helperIndex = 0;` at the top level. What actually happens?
options: ServiceNow throws a duplicate-variable error and blocks both scripts from saving
Both scripts write to the same global-scope variable, and one can silently overwrite the other's value
Each script automatically gets its own private copy of helperIndex
Only the script that saved first will ever run again
questions.explain: Without isolation, both scripts share the page's one global scope, so the same variable name really is the same variable — a silent collision, not an error.

options: The two scripts would merge into a single combined script
ServiceNow would rename one variable automatically
Each script's helperIndex would live in its own sandboxed context, so they'd never touch the same variable
Nothing would change — isolation only affects server-side code
questions.explain: Isolation gives each script its own sandboxed iframe, so identical variable names in two different scripts no longer collide.

questions.q: What is the narrow, legitimate reason to uncheck "Isolate script" on a client script?
options: It makes every client script run noticeably faster
Non-isolated is required for onCellEdit scripts specifically
It's needed any time a script calls GlideAjax
A specific documented need for direct global-scope access, such as certain legacy UI Macro interactions or older integrations
questions.explain: The documented, narrow case is legacy UI Macro interactions or older integrations expecting direct global access — not a general performance or convenience choice.

questions.q: What's the standing rule this lesson teaches for new client scripts?
options: Never isolate, since isolation always breaks g_form access
Isolate by default; only disable isolation when a specific, documented need requires it
Isolate only onCellEdit scripts, never onLoad or onChange
Isolation is deprecated and no longer configurable
questions.explain: Isolation is the safe default because it prevents naming collisions and improves stability and security; exceptions should be rare and documented.
